source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Assess pain, fatigue, emotional state, motivation, language and health-literacy needs, then choose timing and teaching methods accordingly.","B":"Assess only years of formal education because current symptoms, stress, language and motivation do not materially affect learning.","C":"Teach immediately whenever staff time is available, even if pain, fatigue or distress prevents the client from attending to the information.","D":"Skip readiness assessment because hospitalized adults can absorb and retain the same amount of information at any point during illness."}}
source_row.rationale: Effective patient education is individualized to the patient's ability to engage and understand; symptoms, distress, fatigue, language, motivation and health-literacy needs influence timing and method.
source_row.source_detail: Tool 12 / patient education guidance: assess understanding, use patient-centered communication and teach-back, and adapt education to the patient's needs and ability to engage. AHRQ Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit page rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: Before discharge teaching, which assessment best determines a client's readiness and ability to learn?
